claims.proposedDisposition: Recommend a direct, symmetric conservative exclusion for this pair to protect the broad displayed label 'mark' against the independently attested grave-marker extension of 墓. This is a precaution about the overlapping referent and broad quiz label, not a claim that 標 ordinarily means grave or that all marks/signposts are graves.

displayedLabelDirections.標_on_墓: The standalone 標/しるし mark/sign and the displayed 'mark' can describe a marker; independently, はか includes an actual grave marker. Some grave markers are mark-like physical objects. A generic mark is not necessarily a grave.
displayedLabelDirections.墓_on_標: A grave or its marker can be a mark in a specific burial setting, although 'grave; tomb' is not a general definition of 標. The pair guard is symmetric to prevent the same limited ambiguity in either direction, without treating broad signs, standards, guidance or goals as graves.

positiveEvidence: Reused 日本国語大辞典 full capture at ../survey-001/external/墓-kotobank.txt:123-129: はか includes grave monuments and grave markers, as well as a burial place.

external/標-weblio.txt:37-65, 183-207: Digital Daijisen's しるし entry includes 標, describes marks used for identification/signalling, and lists 墓標 as a compound; spelling marks and other entry senses must be retained.

external/標-kotobank.txt:25-66, 120-180, 228-258: Digital Daijisen, 日本国語大辞典 and 字通 give independent broad marks, marker posts, target and other senses, with examples and distinct historical registers; none requires reading grave into standalone 標.

jmdict-exact-families.xml:4-64 entry 1168060: しるし family has the exact spelling 標; mark/sign senses specify esp. 印, 標, while evidence/proof senses specify 証, 証し. Other senses and spelling restrictions remain present.

jmdict-exact-families.xml:301-343 entry 1514900 and external/墓標-kotobank.txt:25-51, 65-112: 墓標 is a whole word for a marker, and ぼひょう also has an inscription sense; はかじるし reading is spelling-restricted in JMdict.
kanjidic2-exact-characters.xml:79-158 retains the complete 標 character record and its mark/signpost/target and other meanings; it does not gloss 標 as grave.
claims.minimalChangeIfAdjudicated: Append 標 to 墓's existing quiz_exclusions and add a single narrowly qualified Notes explanation. Under the existing direct-pair symmetric rule, do not independently edit 標 or propagate any exclusion transitively.
claims.counterEvidenceAndLimits: A shared compound character or a compound's full gloss does not by itself prove an independent grave sense of 標. The recommendation rests on the actual native-word marker extension plus 標's independent broad mark sense, not solely on 墓標 or current curated exposure.

claims.proposedDisposition: Recommend a direct, symmetric conservative exclusion to protect the broad tower/pagoda label against evidenced grave-marker/tomb-like tower forms. This is a specific funerary overlap, not a claim that all 塔 or all 仏塔 are graves, or that 供養塔 always denotes a grave.

displayedLabelDirections.塔_on_墓: Some stone pagodas/towers function as grave markers or graves. A 'tower; pagoda' option can therefore describe some monuments that the independent はか sources include; most towers and religious memorials need not be graves.
displayedLabelDirections.墓_on_塔: An actual stupa or stone tower may contain remains or serve as a grave; 'grave; tomb' can describe those particular structures. This does not turn a secular steeple, each Buddhist tower, a tablet or a mere memorial into a grave.

positiveEvidence: external/塔-kotobank.txt:25-75, 120-140: Digital Daijisen and 日本国語大辞典 separately define standalone 塔 as a Buddhist relic/worship structure and a tall tower. The latter's word history describes an original Indian burial mound/grave; this historical statement is not unqualified proof that ordinary modern 塔 means grave.

jmdict-exact-families.xml:73-103 entry 1446740: 塔/とう has tower/steeple/spire plus a separately labelled original-meaning abbreviation sense stupa/pagoda/dagoba; jmdict-exact-families.xml:224-240 entry 1502260 defines the whole 仏塔 word as stupa/pagoda.

external/仏塔-kotobank.txt:25-56, 70-105: Digital Daijisen and 日本国語大辞典 describe a tower housing Buddha's remains; Nipponica describes a stupa as a grave place and its mound/tower development. That evidence covers certain physical referents rather than all modern pagodas.

external/石塔-kotobank.txt:25-43, 52-96: Digital Daijisen and 日本国語大辞典 include a stone Buddhist tower used as a grave and separately a stone grave marker; jmdict-referenced-families.xml:38-55 entry 1703230 includes both stone tower/pagoda and gravestone senses of the whole 石塔 word.

external/仏塔-kotobank.txt:148 records five-ring and Hōkyōin stone pagodas used as grave markers or memorial towers; external/墓標-kotobank.txt:84-98 includes both 卒塔婆 and 五輪の塔 among markers. jmdict-exact-families.xml:586-599 entry 2843930 identifies 五輪塔 as a five-part gravestone.

external/塔婆-kotobank.txt:47-80: 日本国語大辞典 explicitly gives a grave-tablet sense and, broadly, grave/marker for 塔婆. jmdict-exact-families.xml:105-127 entry 1446750 gives stupa/pagoda and wooden grave tablet; jmdict-referenced-families.xml:4-36 entry 1596620 retains the distinct senses and spelling/reading restrictions of 卒塔婆.
external/卒塔婆-kotobank.txt:145-150 Nipponica distinguishes the modern grave-side board from a building ordinarily called 塔. Do not automatically transfer the full 塔婆 tablet/墓 sense to standalone 塔.

Reused ../survey-001/external/墓-kotobank.txt:337-353 Nipponica distinguishes ordinary 供養塔 and other memorial facilities from 墓 while separately explaining specific grave-marker forms developed from towers.
claims.minimalChangeIfAdjudicated: Append 塔 to 墓's existing quiz_exclusions and add a single qualified Notes explanation distinguishing some burial/marker towers from towers and memorial structures generally. Under the existing direct-pair symmetric rule, do not separately modify 塔 or propagate exclusions.
claims.counterEvidenceAndLimits: KANJIDIC2 and JMdict do not give an unrestricted ordinary 'grave' gloss for standalone 塔; the actual evidence includes historically qualified and whole-compound senses. A topic association alone is insufficient. Here native-source definitions identify specific tower-shaped grave and marker objects, supporting a conservative broad-label guard, not universal synonymy.

sourceDisclosures: Initial exact JMdict spelling query matches 23 complete families; the referenced-term query matches five, including a duplicate five-ring family with equal canonical hash, for 27 distinct families. No contains or exact-reading query is claimed.

An exact JMdict 墓塔 spelling query has zero matches in this pinned snapshot. Do not infer universal absence or a lexical definition from either.

標/ひょう rare flag and historical courts/seating senses are preserved as labelled; native しるし is a separate complete family with spelling restrictions. No claim is made that every alternate spelling applies equally to every sense.
